Hey Radek, thanks for your feedback!

The new process was introduced because we noticed that CSAT for this issue was very low on a global level. We found that markets that actually call drivers have higher CSAT and that’s one reason we implemented this step globally. Also, it doesn’t really matter that much what item the rider lost - if they reported it to us, we should try to help them get their item back.

The step to let the rider know that they are responsible for their belongings was removed because it brings no value to the customer. Yes, it’s your fault as a customer that you’ve lost your item but you reach out to support to get help, not to be reminded that it was your fault.

Why we no longer advise the rider to contact the driver on their own if it’s less than 24 hrs is because:

* If it’s less than 24 hrs, riders get an automation that advises them to call the driver.
* Additionally, prior to sending a ticket they may read a self-help article that tells them the same thing.
* Thus, it doesn’t make sense for us to provide them with the same solution for the 3rd time and since they already made an effort to contact us, we should take ownership over resolving the issue.

I hope it answers your questions but let me know if you have some other questions 🙂

Hey, [~accountid:5bb1cc64c9dad04734ea835a]! Can you please help to understand me more about this issue:

Clause 6.3 of the [General Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/1dmPNGREwp1sPayZ2PdIhj/68959db2012dd99722ec88d10f1540e4/Global_-_General_Terms_and_Conditions_for_Bolt_Business__effective_from_01.03.2023_.pdf] states that Bolt will not be liable for certain issues and one of them is “loss of data” outlined in 6.3.2. The customer here objects to having this exclusion by saying that:

{quote}”In our opinion, this data is most likely covered by the personal data protection regime under the GDPR, and it seems to us a tendency to circumvent the obligations of the data controller under the GDPR.”{quote}

We have tried to argue this using the commentary from the [Playbook|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923659743/Contracting+playbook+for+Bolt+s+General+Business+Portal+T+C.+Team+Account+Ride+Booker.+Standard+Customers], but it was not sufficient. However, when drivers raise this ATI, they usually have already taken the step described in the automation.

If a driver reaches out for this ATI and any KPI metrics are high, the root causes could be:



* The driver is missing a specific document (the driver added the vehicle, yet it hasn't been approved. This often involves market-specific back-and-forth conversations about which documents are needed). A good example is here: [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/249667262|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/249667262]
* The driver is inquiring about the duration of the vehicle application process. This issue is linked to the car application backlog in South Africa and Thailand.



S*uggested solutions:*

* Once the driver clicks "No" after encountering the automation, another prompt could appear: _"If you have already registered your car in the Driver Portal, please provide us with the registration number. This will allow us to offer you the best possible support._"
* If we possess this information and agents are instructed to review the car applications before sending responses like the one in this example ([https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/239667685|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/239667685]), we can genuinely assist the driver and offer more precise feedback regarding the car applications. This can be particularly important for markets where the car application rejection rate might be high (I don’t have data for this yet).

Regarding lat/lng coordinates, currently they are in the raw format as we have them in internal databases.

I see two approaches possible here:

# We round the precision of the coordinates. For example, divide the city into a square grid with roughly ~200-400 metres cell side length. Each trip that starts from a square gets its coordinates snapped to the centre of the square. This is effectively somewhere between *pseudonymized* and *anonymized* - in theory it’s possible for some remote squares (villa in the suburbs) to cross-reference a house’s owner with trips originating from there. But this is only possible for selected trips.
# We could do 1. and then further filter out squares with very sparse activity - for example less than N trips in a time period. This way filters out the villa in the suburbs scenario and furthermore - no individual should be possible to be identified. This should effectively be *anonymized* data?

Query to get a list of next candidates:

rules are:

* not custom pricing (for now)
* at least 5% of orders get to 4th order try (proxy for size of FOO opportunity)
* at least 1000 of the above in last 2 months
* sort by {{share_4plus_OT * (finished_rate - finished_rate_4plus_OT) desc}} which is size of opportunity x size of potential effect on finished rate
* take up to 2 per country
* ignore lightweight markets for now

{noformat}-- FOO candidates query
with cp_cities as (
    select distinct
        last_city_id
    from glue.pricing.driver_pricing
    where true
        and created_hour > date('2023-06-22')
        and state = 'custom_pricing'
),
ot as (
    select
        city_id,
        order_id,
        count(*) as ot_count
    from glue.ng_public.company_order_try
    where created_date >= date('2023-06-22')
        and city_id not in (select last_city_id from cp_cities)
        -- already tested
        and city_id not in (336, 32, 55, 393, 812, 438, 375, 1, 496)
        -- explicit exclusions
        -- and city_id not in ()
    group by 1,2
),
agg as (
    select
        co.city_id,
        asc.name,
        country_code,
        avg(case when ot_count > 3 then 1.000 else 0.000 end) as share_4plus_OT,
        sum(case when ot_count > 3 and state = 'finished' then 1.000 else 0.000 end) / (1.000 + sum(case when ot_count > 3 then 1.000 else 0.000 end)) as finished_rate_4plus_OT,
        avg(case when state = 'finished' then 1.000 else 0.000 end) as finished_rate,
        sum(case when ot_count > 3 and not(state = 'finished') then 1 else 0 end) as count_unfinished_4plus_OT,
        count(*) as order_count
    from glue.ng_public.company_order co
    left join ot on (co.id = order_id and co.city_id = ot.city_id)
    left join glue.ng_public.admin_system_city asc on (asc.id = co.city_id)
    where created_date >= date('2023-06-22')
    group by 1,2,3
),
output as (
    select
        *,
        row_number() over (partition by country_code order by share_4plus_OT * (finished_rate - finished_rate_4plus_OT) desc) as country_rank
    from agg
    where count_unfinished_4plus_OT > 1000
    -- and finished_rate_4plus_OT < 0.5
    and share_4plus_OT > 0.05
    -- and finished_rate_4plus_OT < finished_rate - 0.05
)
select
    *
from output
where country_rank < 3
and country_code not in ('th', 'py', 'cy', 'ie')
order by country_code, country_rank
;{noformat}

{noformat}~ >printf Q | openssl s_client -servername payments.bolt.eu -connect payments.bolt.eu:443 | openssl x509 -noout -dates

The issue is actually not in SSL, but in verification file. Apple requires to host domain verification file under {{.well-known/apple-developer-merchantid-domain-association}}. This file is generated in Apple Developer Portal
[https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple_pay_on_the_web/maintaining_your_environment#3179140|https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple_pay_on_the_web/maintaining_your_environment#3179140|smart-link] Two problems can be

* Domain verification file is not hosted and Apple cannot verify domain. I see that currently [payment.bolt.eu|http://payment.bolt.eu/] redirects to [https://static.bolt.eu/payment/3ds/finish3ds.html?result=failure|https://static.bolt.eu/payment/3ds/finish3ds.html?result=failure|smart-link] . Probably Apple just cannot open file due to redirection
* Apple cannot reach {{/.well-known/apple-developer-merchantid-domain-association}}, because their IP addresses are not whitelisted. But seems it’s not the issue, because I can reach [payments.bolt.eu|http://payments.bolt.eu/]. Check this: [https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple_pay_on_the_web/setting_up_your_server#3179116|https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple_pay_on_the_web/setting_up_your_server#3179116|smart-link]

The step to escalate cases to the Local OPS is added to the process if the Issue acts as a Driver Score (BQS) signal. You can see them all in [🚗 Rider issues list|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360020769979], the Issues are marked with “(DS)”. In markets where the BQS is active, the driver behavior data is collected automatically by the Issue tag name, and in the markets without the BQS - Local OPS teams have to be informed manually. 

I understand that your request is to make the escalation process more convenient, but it is important to note that our team strives for global standardization by implementing a consistent approach across all markets. Local process variations are only implemented when they are deemed essential.

In addition to this, Slack escalations are not the best solution, because agents need to copy/paste information from Beehive/Admin, and it increases AHT and THT, also Agent utilization data on escalated tickets is not tracked, escalation data can’t be extracted from Looker, and many other reasons. 

With that being said, can you please elaborate on what are the blockers for the In-house OPS team to use Beehive? Why do you think it wouldn’t be important for OPS to know about the driver issues from the 1st complaint? OPS doesn’t necessarily have to take any action if that’s not needed, but escalation is required for tracking and collecting the data. 

I look forward to hearing your thoughts and continuing this discussion. ☀️

Hi [~accountid:61d554bb68926d00685d572c] and [~accountid:6336b241a84c7f79c387c386],

Ahead of our call tomorrow, I would like to summarise in writing my legal advice and recommendations on how these Bolt Business WhatsApp Communications could be improved from privacy perspective in relation to the transparency requirement and the opt-out right of the individuals.

Although initially, it looked as if the WhatsApp Communications were purely operational or service messages as one could say, after having a closer look at the purpose of these Comms, I could say that we are actually encouraging Admins in the first scenario and Business Users in the second one to activate their accounts and start using our services.

According to the Direct Marketing Guidance by ICO, If you want to send a message that actively promotes or encourages people to make use of a particular service, then it is likely to be direct marketing, whereas a service message is defined as a communication sent to an individual for administrative or customer service purposes only.

In the first scenario, we are addressing the message to prospective customers and actually encouraging them to complete the set up of the Bolt Business Account by either adding company details or payment methods like credit card details.  They are not our customers yet and we don't have a relationship with them to whom we want to send just an administrative or customer service message. So, in fact we are still trying to sell our services. 

In the second scenario, it’s easier to argue that it is about an operational message, since the Business account has been set up, the Business Users have been added and all is missing for the activation is the change of the payment method. If though we continue sending messages to encourage the added Business Users to take a ride, this could also be considered as a marketing message, since we are encouraging them to use a particular service and spend money on it.

Just to add that the ICO in its Direct Marketing Guidance says that “if you have a relationship with a person, the phrasing, tone and context are likely to be a key factor in whether the message you want to send is direct marketing. 
For example, if a message has a neutral tone and simply gives information that they need to know as part of their relationship with you this is more likely to be a service message”. 

Otherwise, there is the risk of the message being perceived as a marketing message.

So, based on this analysis, and especially regarding the first scenario, I would advise the business to seek consent/opt-in from the Admins in order to send WhatsApp Communications.

In case consent is not collected, there is a legal risk of which I would like to make you aware.

I understand though that the collection of consent would have a big impact on the efficiency of these communications and the business has good reasons not to want to collect consent, senior management included, so in this case it would be more of a business decision and a matter of willingness to accept the risk or not.

It’s worth noting as well that as we are dealing with African territories at the moment and not with the UK, where ICO’s guidance applies, the risk is lower and probably the African authorities less strict with these privacy requirements.

Another message will follow with the wording recommendations.

Best and see you tomorrow,

Melina

*Updated Guidance from Local Counsel*:

*Portugal*

_Is there a particular reason why a GDPR level of consent is required? Is it the Local Counsels view that the Criminal Code's definition of consent in Article 38 is substantially similar to the requirements in the GDPR?_

Yes. Article 38 of the Criminal Code defines consent as one of the grounds for the exemption of illegality and fault as far as criminal liability is concerned in relation to the recording of other persons, and the definition of consent in Article 38 is substantially similar to the requirements in the GDPR. In addition, a GDPR level of consent will be required from a data protection law perspective as personal data will be captured through the audio-recording, and under Portuguese law consent would be the only valid legal basis for such an activity.

_We would like to clarify whether the Local Counsel views this consent as being required every time the feature is used, or whether it would be sufficient to obtain this level of consent on a once-off basis?_

Strictly speaking, GDPR level of consent is required every time the +*feature*+ is used. This is because data subjects (drivers, passengers and additional passengers) must make an informed decision every time they use the feature. If the driver, passenger or additional passenger does not provide their consent then Bolt may not record. Furthermore, following consent being obtained, a signal (such as a notification or pop up, ideally with a sound) should be made available to all recorded parties when the recording starts, so they are all aware.

Alternatively, on a risk based approach, Bolt can obtain a GDPR level of consent on a one-off basis from both the driver and passenger, when first using the +*app*+, so long as, for those who have consented, a notification is shown every time the +*feature*+ is used is used which allows them to reconfirm their original consent or withdraw. For those who did not give their consent when first using the +*app*+, the feature should not be available to be used on any trip. If both the driver and passenger reconfirm their consent for the use of the +*feature*+, a signal (such as another notification or pop up, again ideally with a sound) should be made available when the recording starts, so they are both aware. If the passenger or driver withdraws their original consent then Bolt may not record. Please note, this alternative approach does not provide for additional passengers to give their consent, which as stated above is required every time the feature is used to comply with local law.

Where consent is obtained, this consent must be freely given, specific, informed (including informing users of the possibility to withdraw or reconfirm consent in any trip and where all individuals do consent to the recording, that a notification will be displayed to signal that the audio-recording has begun etc.) and an unambiguous indication of the data subject's wishes, but also be compliant with article 6 of the GDPR and considering that sensitive data may be involved, it must be explicit under article 9(2)(a) GDPR.

In summary, Local Counsel's recommendations to Bolt are:

# (i) Collect consent from all parties (driver, passenger and each additional passenger) to be recorded every time one of the users (driver or passenger) chooses to use the feature; and (ii) where all parties (driver, passenger and each additional passenger) confirm their consent then a warning (ideally with sound) pop-ups to notify when the recording has started so all parties (driver, passenger and each additional passenger) are aware OR
# (i) Collect initial consent from all users (driver and passenger) to be recorded when they first use the app, then (ii) for those who have previously consented, another pop up will ask all users (driver and passenger) to reconfirm their consent or withdraw it every time one of the users (driver or passenger) chooses to use the feature and (iii) where all users (driver and passenger) reconfirm their consent then a warning (ideally with sound) pop-ups to notify when the recording has started so all parties (driver, passenger and each additional passenger) are aware. This option will only be possible for app users, which means that for additional passengers Bolt must ensure that their consent is obtain every time the feature is used.

Investigated issue on our side, the use cases tested using the Android app in prelive (issue is reported on iOS though):

# Started sign up and stopped at email screen. Looked for corresponding provisional login in DB, set its creation date >7 days ago. Killed the app, reopened it and I’m getting to the Sign In screen. I managed to recreate the issue, but the provisional login should expire sometime between the first attempt and the second one.
# Started sign up and stopped at email screen. Changed corresponding provisional login status from {{PENDING_SIGNUP}} (normal behaviour) to {{COMPLETE}} to test with an invalid state. After killing the app I’m redirected to the Sign in screen. Clicking on Sign In in this case shows an error prompt.
# Created a situation where multiple provisional logins match a particular phone_uuid, in which case the algorithm takes the oldest valid provisional login regardless of status. Tested the following:
## if provisional login returned for getAppState is “pending phone verification”, the flow shows the OTP screen.
## if provisional login is pending sign up, normal flow, user is shown the email screen
## if provisional login is pending _email_ verification app crashes 😅 
## if provisional login is complete, app shows the sign in screen. Clicking on sign in shows an error message with “something went wrong”.
# Changing {{phone_uuid}} between app state calls will prevent the device to match to any provisional login so, when relaunching the app it is normal to be redirected to the sign in screen.

In conclusion, I managed to recreate this issue when:

# Phone UUID changes between calls, the issue is expected behaviour since we cannot match the device with any existing provisional logins.
# Provisional login expires between calls or the device is enrolled in different groups of the provisional login experiment, so the eligible matching provisional logins between calls will change.

Hi [~accountid:5df755169422830caca9f633] - see below regarding the payment system and the amount the driver receives for each journey.

Bolt is the provider of the transport services available via our platform (since 1st August 2022). Therefore:

* Passengers contract directly with Bolt (rather than drivers) for the provision of the transport services.

* Passengers pay Bolt directly for journeys taken via our platform.

* The driver contracts with Bolt to fulfil journeys on Bolt’s behalf. Bolt pays the driver a “Journey Fee” which will be shown in the driver app. 

* Bolt receives the payment and then paying the driver, rather than the passenger paying the driver and Bolt applying a commission.

Reconciliation between TR EIB and PSP settlement is hard. The data granularity is different, and some breakdowns within a single TR transaction might go to different PSP settlements. For example, a single chargeback row in TR EIB might have different components, such as (a) dispute fee and (b) actual chargeback. Components (a) and (b) might go to different settlements in different months.

Reversed reconciliation from the PSP side is also not straightforward. Any single breakdown could be mapped to a particular TR EIB transaction, but the amount couldn’t be reconciled. 

Even if that’s possible, the other complexity comes from the fact that withdrawal is not always the sum of all payments in a single settlement. Withdrawal might come from outstanding balance from previous settlement, making it more complicated.

Art. 14 of the EU Regulation 1169/2011 provides that in the case of prepacked foods offered for sale by means of distance communication, the responsible food business operator is required to make available all mandatory food information, except for the date of minimum durability or the ‘use by’ date before the purchase is concluded.

Mandatory food information includes the information concerning the presence of allergens listed in Annex II of the Regulation. I have noticed that many stores have already added this information to the product description on the Bolt Food app.

Even though it is the responsibility of restaurants/stores to provide this information, if the inspection launches an investigation, the platform operator that enabled distance selling will be held liable, too (discussed this over the phone with Food and Veterinary Service in Latvia).

To ensure compliance, it is advised to: 

# send a notice to all the stores requiring them to add manually (unless they have a link that directs to the information on the official website of the store) mandatory information about the products they are selling, including allergens, as required by Regulation 1169/2011;
# If this is not done by a specific date, we reserve the right to suspend the store/restaurant from the platform in accordance with Art.8.2 of T&C for Partners.

This obligation stems from the EU law, therefore is applicable to all the EU countries.

Yes, frugality is important but so is our user experience, so we should keep both in mind. This year, Markus has been emphasizing quality a lot too and this applies to quality of support as well. In a nutshell, if we are losing our users due to their poor experience with our products and support, then it’s bad for business and it doesn’t matter if we are doing things efficiently if we are not doing things effectively in the first place (as in not providing users with the best service possible).

We don’t know if the process will increase AHT. In fact, we’ve removed some unnecessary steps from the process which should have a positive impact on AHT. Also, the new step to call the driver should actually allow us to solve cases faster as we don’t need to wait for driver’s response to a written message. If a driver starts asking you about something that doesn’t relate to this specific case, then you should ask them to open a separate case on this matter.

In any case, you can be sure that we will monitor the process to see how it performs globally and locally by checking data and gathering feedback from CS Ops team. If we see that the process doesn’t perform as expected, we’ll adjust it.

-Data about the usage of the transportation services: things like data about journey status, times and data about your conduct as assessed by drivers.

-Profile information: things like your profile picture, saved addresses, language and communication preferences. For some of our services we might require a little more, like your driver license details.

-Geolocation: such as where you need a ride from, or the location of nearby scooters to you, the time, the journey progression and the final destination of your trip.

I could also see these stats falling potentially under the following *purpose:*

*We maintain and promote standards:* We collect data about journey statuses, time and passenger ratings from driver feedback to encourage user safety, promote compliance with our terms and conditions, and make sure we’re providing a quality and enjoyable service to everyone. -We generally in other circumstances process your personal data relying on legitimate interest grounds. (Our legitimate interests also include things like investigating and detecting fraudulent payments and other malicious activities, maintaining the security of our network and systems, and responding to suspected or actual criminal acts).

Hi [~accountid:61cc1c959ee70a00680edd89] and [~accountid:625fb4921046bb0071ddf448] , 

In ITA data can be requested by: 

*  *the Police* for traffic and parking rules, 
*  by the *Municipality* (in the case at stake, Milan) as per local rules imposed over car sharing operators. 
* *Regulators and authorities* for law enforcement purposes
* *Zity* to ensure legal defense in the framework of legal proceeding against users. 

I’m sharing my comments re each data point listed in the draft agreement. 

* Full name (first name, last name): mandatory info for Zity to operate the service. 
* Date of birth:  mandatory info for Zity to operate the service and make sure that only adult age users accesse the services.  Zity may also need to share aggregate data re users age to the Municipality.
* Gender: Zity might need to share aggregate data regarding gender ratio of users (% women vs men).
* City:  not mandatory 
* Place of birth: not mandatory unless requested by local authorities. 
* Nationality: not mandatory unless requested by local authorities for law enforcement purposes. 
* Address (ZIP and Country included): can be requested by authorities to Zity for law enforcement purposes including parking fines which are usually notified by mail to the residency address. 
* Email address : not mandatory unless requested by local authorities or for CS purposes. 
* Tax Code (Codice Fiscale): not mandatory unless requested by local authorities ( Tax Authority)
* Mobile Phone number (including international prefix): not mandatory unless requested by local authorities.
* Driver License information (DL number, expiration date, first emission date, and front & back images of the document) : this is mandatory info for Zity to operate the service. 
* ID information (including ID number, date of issue, expiration date and front & back images of the document) : not mandatory unless requested by local authorities.
* Operator T&C and Private Policy acceptance (evidence and date and hour of the acceptance) : can be requested by regulators and in the event of legal proceedings against users. 
* Any other that may be legally enforceable : too broad.

Please let me know if you need further help. 

Best regards, 

Michela

*“Driver reports that the rider refused multiple destinations.*

*Note:* Editing destinations and adding stops are currently available for drivers only in some markets. Therefore, some drivers won't see this option in the app. Please consult your Local OPS team if unsure whether the feature is available.

Follow the procedure below if a driver complains that a rider refused to change the destination, resulting in the price not recalculating.

*Step 1: Verify the order*

* Check the route map to confirm that what has been reported matches the order and that the driver did finish the trip at a different place.
* If yes, educate the driver on how to change the final destination in the app on behalf of the rider and proceed to Step 2.
* If no, inform the driver that the order information matches the original destination and skip the following steps.
* For markets where drivers cannot change the destination, proceed to Step 2.

*Step 2*: *Follow up on the report*

* Apologize to the driver about the situation.
* If not already given, ask the driver about the reason why the rider refused to change the destination.
* Decide whether to compensate or not, depending on your market rules.
* Leave a comment on the rider’s profile.”

h3. {color:#36b37e}Feature summary{color}

*Riders will be able to upload their profile picture and this feature will increase driver safety and equalize the information riders & drivers know about each other.*

* Riders will be able to upload their picture after the account is created - Menu → Profile → Tap on photo. There will be guidelines for appropriate pictures. Riders will be able to delete & edit their picture. It won’t be mandatory to upload it. Rider’s picture will be shown in Admin but {color:#bf2600}_it will require specific permission_{color}.
* Driver will see the picture only when they are 500m close to the pickup point. Photo won’t be shown in trip history or receipts, drivers won’t be able to save it. 
* Probably drivers won’t be able to cancel the order if the picture doesn’t match, because riders can order rides for other people, however, drivers should still be able to cancel rides if they don’t feel safe or the picture is inappropriate. {color:#bf2600}_Check if it will be decided to add a new cancellation reason._ {color}
* If the rider’s photo is flagged as inappropriate, the account should be manually reviewed by CS and if that’s confirmed - the account should be manually blocked (sexually explicit, hate speech, violence). 

*So far, it seems that we need:*

* General feature KB article with guidelines (what is this feature; type of complaints; how to respond)
* A process for drivers reporting inappropriate pictures / CS agents noticing those pictures.
* Update drivers' content related to order cancellations (if this feature will change anything)

I agree with [~accountid:610279973900e60070a3495c]. 23% makes no sense at all in this case. When it comes to rebates in resale markets like Portugal, there’s always an original sale to which a certain VAT rate applies, we either discount it or credit it. In both cases, the VAT rate of the rebate must always match the VAT rate of the original sale it relates to, whatever it is/was. 

So, in fact, “Rebate VAT” is not something that should exist as a distinct setting. Given our current setup, and IF rebates indeed only apply to Rides, then matching “rebate VAT” to “rides VAT” in Portugal should give the correct outcome, as a workaround. So: set “Rebate VAT” to 6%. 

But if we rebate our service fee, 23% should apply, if we rebate car sharing 23% should apply. Fact is: system should be smart enough to check what’s being rebated and apply correct VAT treatment accordingly. [~accountid:712020:2432bf62-c6bc-4b10-85a8-ef21c78a1e56] So I suggest doing a full review of rebates, defining proper business logic (with help from our tax lawyers where needed), then taking this up with our engineers. 

FYI[~accountid:625fb4941046bb0071ddf44a] has recently reviewed our rebate setup in Intermediary, here [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CKGKGPZUM/p1692359950038259|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CKGKGPZUM/p1692359950038259|smart-link]. If there’s nothing to discount or credit (a situation that doesn’t apply to a resale market like Portugal), the transaction would be out of scope of VAT. In an intermediary market, our rebate doesn’t apply to our own sales, but to our partner’s sales. In that scenario, we’ll be paying our customers for using our platform / to pay part of the invoices sent to them by our partners.

Strimzi has lots of different certificates for communication among different components. All of them are created by the operator during cluster creation time. They are self-signed by an internal certificate authorities. Renewal process is managed completely by Strimzi.

* Cluster CA - used to sign a bunch of different certificates (e.g. for brokers, zookeepers, topic/user operator). Since all of them are self-signed, this CA should be added to client truststore if native certificates are going to be used for TLS listeners. Since we plan to use cert-manager provided certificates for TLS listeners we don’t need to do anything with this CA.
* Client CA - used to sign the certificates of client applications for mTLS. We won’t use mTLS, so not important for us.

Hi team, I think I might have found the root cause of the issue.

The issue seems to stem from the usage of the Work Profile.

As I see it, Bolt has started to report Bolt Drive Work Profile invoices to the Lithuanian tax authorities.

There are some different dynamics at play here.

Take, for example, this company: [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/business-invoicing/businessCompanies/edit/263046?tab=business_company|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/business-invoicing/businessCompanies/edit/263046?tab=business_company]
This user: [https://admin.bolt.eu/user/users/user/29138387|https://admin.bolt.eu/user/users/user/29138387] chose to use the Work Profile, but as a payment method for the Work Profile, he is using the company’s payment method. 

As a result, we see that the invoice was created under his company’s name because he was using company's payment method.

Since our users generally are not able to differentiate between two business products (Work Profile and Business Team account), sometimes they just use both of them, as Bolt app allows it.

To help you understand better, I attached an example from my Bolt app, showing exactly what this user did - he chose the Work Profile and Team account at the same time. That’s why we reported to the Lithuanian tax authorities these two particular invoices in addition to the monthly business invoice.

!IMG_7956.png|width=1170,height=2532!



Another company with the same issue, but slightly different issue pattern: [https://admin.bolt.eu/business/BusinessCompany/company/72884|https://admin.bolt.eu/business/BusinessCompany/company/72884]

LOCUS.MB company has  a business account, but one of their employees used Work Profile for his trip and as a payment method used a bank card that is added as a personal card directly in his Bolt App. 

User: [https://admin.bolt.eu/user/users/user/25245558|https://admin.bolt.eu/user/users/user/25245558]

We still reported the invoice to the Lithuanian tax authorities, but this time the invoice is with the company’s name and not Bolt (as the payment method is not synced with Business Portal).

Bolt Drive order: [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals-carsharing/orders/edit/global/8408980?tab=details|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals-carsharing/orders/edit/global/8408980?tab=details]

This trip has not been added to the monthly invoice or in the CSV report.

So basically, we have these two scenarios of the issue circulating because Bolt Drive started to report Work Profile invoices to the Lithuanian tax authorities. 

This setup seems really problematic because of these points:

# Most clients are not able to separate Work Profile and Business Team account. And this is a huge issue that should be escalated to the product - we should not let users use Work Profile with the Team Account's payment method as I showed in the picture with my App.

2. Another concern, since we do not authorize Work Profile details. In Kafka, we have separate topics for search events and order events. However, in a Spark job, all the topics are read at the same time as one stream:

{code:python}spark.readStream \
.format("kafka") \
.option("subscribe", "sqs.search_event, sqs.order_event") \
.load()
...
.withWatermark("event_time", "15 seconds"){code}

This creates a potential for data issues if one topic stops behaving properly. Spark wouldn’t wait until this topic goes back to a normal state as there will be just one watermark on the stream.

A solution to this issue is to create multiple streams, a separate one for each topic:


{noformat}stream1 = spark.readStream \
  .format("kafka") \
  .option("subscribe", "sqs.search_event") \
  .load()
  ...
  .withWatermark("event_time", "15 seconds")
  
stream2 = spark.readStream \
  .format("kafka") \
  .option("subscribe", "sqs.order_event") \
  .load()
  ...
  .withWatermark("event_time", "15 seconds")
  
df = stream1.union(stream2){noformat}

In this setup, there will be two watermarks assigned to each of the stream and the global watermark (used for stateful operations) will move with the _slowest_ watermark. If one stream stops producing data, Spark will effectively wait until it goes back to a normal state without the risk of outputting incorrect data.

[~accountid:60c88e6e8f2cc1006909fcf6] the summary:

Until 2019, Bolt Technology OÜ had a registered permanent establishment in Latvia with a purpose to provide supporting activities to Bolt Technology OÜ in Estonia (later the LV permanent establishment was replaced by a LV subsidiary). The permanent establishment paid taxes in Latvia on the profits which were corresponding to the support functions performed by the permanent establishment as per OECD methodology of attributing the profits to permanent establishments.

Latvian State Revenue Services (SRS) took the position that all the revenues earned by Bolt Technology OÜ from Latvia should be allocated to the permanent establishment notwithstanding whether the functions to generate these revenues were performed by the employees of Latvian permanent establishment or the employees of Estonian HQ. 

Bolt disagrees to the approach taken by the SRS as in our view this approach is not in compliance with the double tax treaty concluded between Estonia and Latvia.Bolt has challenged this approach in Latvian Courts. Estonian tax authorities have confirmed that the approach taken by Latvian tax authorities leads potentially to double taxation. Consequently also a Mutual Agreement Procedure (MAP) has been initiated to have Estonian and Latvian tax authorities to agree on a mutual interpretation of the double tax treaty with a purpose to avoid double taxation to a Bolt as a taxpayer . The Court proceedings in Latvia have been suspended until the results of the MAP Proceedings between the tax authorities.

Although disagreeing to SRS's position, it's important to note that Bolt has fulfilled its obligations by paying all outstanding fines and taxes to the Latvian State Revenue Services, demonstrating our commitment to adhering to legal requirements. We hope the MAP and/or Court proceedings to demonstrate that SRS claim was not justified.

* Paste the driver ID to the Client ID column
* Scroll to the right side and click on the pencil icon to check the status of the payout in question
* Choose the relevant drop-down based on your findings:

*Payout is requested*

This status means that the payout has not been transmitted to the provider. The most common reason for this status is that the driver doesn't have all the required banking details on the profile.

* Advise the driver that they need to update their banking details – follow the [Driver Requests Changing Banking Details|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/internal/360013903520] process

*Payout is blocked as too big*

This status means that the payment was blocked due to the sum being too big.

* Inform the driver that the payout should need to pass the internal check. Submit the ticket _On-Hold._
* Escalate the case to the Commerce Fraud team via [the Service Desk|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/57/create/308] (choose the RH Fraud Issue _Unblock a driver_)
* Await for the response and advise the driver accordingly.

*Payout was too small*

* If the payout was too small, advise the driver accordingly
* Inform them that they will receive a payout in the next payment cycle if their balance is positive and above the local threshold

*Payout is rejected (deleted)*

This status means that the payout was rejected/deleted by the Commerce Partner Payment team due to their operational procedure.

Read the _details_ to check the reason why the payout was rejected/deleted.

*UK:* Escalate any rejected payouts to the Local OPS along with the narrative.

# *NARR: Beneficiary Name is not valid. It contains invalid characters. Please re-enter.*

*Reason:* Invalid characters or probably due to copy-pasting or other reasons resulting in incorrect text formatting.

*Solution:* Ask the driver to correct their banking details accordingly. Follow the [Driver Requests Changing Banking Details |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013903520]process.

*2. NARR:* *Beneficiary Address is not valid. It contains invalid characters. Please re-enter.*

*Reason:* Invalid characters (such as &) or probably due to copy-pasting or other reasons causing incorrect text format.

*Solution:* Ask the driver to correct their banking details accordingly. Follow the [Driver Requests Changing Banking Details |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013903520]process.

*3. NARR: Rejected by Beneficiary Bank.*

*Reason:* Most likely rejected by Beneficiary Bank due to issues with driver's bank account (e.g., closed/blocked).

*Solution:* Advise the driver to contact their bank.

4. *Returned VALUE DATE-YYYY-MM-DD.*

*Reason:* Most likely returned by Beneficiary Bank due to problems with driver's bank account (e.g., closed/blocked).

*Solution:* Advise the driver to contact their bank.

*5. Sorting code is not set.*

*Reason:* Sorting code missing from “Account SWIFT” field on Driver profile.

*Solution:* Ask the driver to correct their banking details accordingly. Follow the [Driver Requests Changing Banking Details |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013903520]process.

*6. Sorting code is invalid. Sorting code must contain 6 digits.*

*Reason:* Sorting code incorrect in “Account SWIFT” field on Driver profile.

*Solution:* Ask the driver to correct their banking details accordingly. Follow the [Driver Requests Changing Banking Details |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013903520]process.

*7. Invalid Beneficiary Bank Routing Code.*

*Reason:* Sorting code incorrect in “Account SWIFT” field on Driver profile.

*Solution:* Ask the driver to correct their banking details accordingly. Follow the [Driver Requests Changing Banking Details |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013903520]process.

*8*. *Additional information: EMPTY.*

*Reason:* Payout subject lacks a valid account IBAN.

*Solution:* Ask the driver to correct their banking details accordingly.  Follow the [Driver Requests Changing Banking Details |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013903520]process.

* This is a case of a company that is owing us €3878 for almost a year
* They used us in intermediary model but at certain point this amount was blocked due to internal policies conflict: they cannot pay to one entity whilst being invoiced by others (fleets)
* For these past months, we tried to clear this debt following our regular processes but we cannot reach an agreement. They are contractually bound to pay us under this format but they simply won’t
* They accept to pay if the invoice comes from Bolt. Commerce is not able to issue credit notes on these individual invoices and reissue a single one from Bolt, thus this ad-hoc request
* We understand that by issuing a new invoice for the same value, they would have two due payments to Bolt but that’s a fiscal risk on their side
* Furthermore, this overdue debt is blocking new business with them (ca. €10k pm as long as they have single invoice)

Our options:

* We send them this ad-hoc invoice and,
** we have debt cleared
** we start new business of ca. €10k pm
** past individual invoices up to €3878 will remain issued but no payment will be done for those
* We don’t raise this invoice and,
** we remain with €3878 in debt that will never be cleared
** we jeopardize new business of ca. €10k pm
** past individual invoices up to €3878 will remain issued but no payment will be done for those

 

Despite understanding that our request may bypass our regular processes, it is given that in any of the scenarios past individual invoices up to €3878 will remain issued but no payment will be done for those. In that sense and weighting our options, we assume this request makes sense.

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

Unless it is our mistake, e.g. the value, subject of the sale, or NIP number is wrongly stated by us, then we reissue the invoice. And we need to report VAT for the new invoice.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

Sharing the result of the 1st investigation. 

The key issue here is that we don’t have the information about the ride while we are checking policies, and therefore all events related to the rides will require a “best match” to the approval.

The ride creation is not even triggered by the service that checks for existing approvals (business-user), once for the rides system the business-user service is just a facade that will validate or not a {{create ride request}}.

To proceed with this task we have to assume that we can somehow match the approval of a user to the ride, and than it becomes easier.
We have some flaws in the current design, once we mark approvals as used before we even finish the check for payment (as a hack we added it to the last step of the check, but it is just until a new policy comes and someone adds it to the end by mistake).

I am proposing an idea to solve the architectural design, as well as a “quick fix” which I don’t recommend, but that will could make the current solution a little bit better, avoiding problems during on the ride creating to result in approvals to be used.

The diagram below has the current, best and “fast track” solutions described:

h3. *_How to decide if compensation is necessary?_*

* _Evaluate the seriousness of the situation based on the user’s report and your investigation_
** _E.g. for RH or Rentals, determine if the user got to their desired destination_
* _Evaluate the dissatisfaction of the user based on their report_
* _Take the risk type of the event into account_
** _E.g. Regular events might not make the user feel as unsafe as High or Significant events_

It was agreed together with the Safety and the Risk and Safety teams that when dealing with safety events, the highest priority is to ensure the user is safe and that we take relevant action on the reported party. Compensation is a second priority, which means we’re unable to give specific instructions on where and when to refund, as each case is different. This is mentioned in the article too:

_When dealing with safety cases, the highest priority is to solve the user’s issue and ensure they’re safe. Compensations are a second priority._

Therefore, when dealing with Safety events and deciding about the compensation, please refer to the guidelines to determine whether compensation is necessary.

        ci = CausalImpact(data[['ds','y_test'] + counterfactuals].set_index('ds'), 
                        train_period, test_period, alpha=alpha,
                        model_args = model_arg)
        
        actual = ci.summary_data.loc['actual']['average']
        predicted = ci.summary_data.loc['predicted']['average']
        abs_effect = ci.summary_data.loc['abs_effect']['average']
        pred_lower_ci = ci.summary_data.loc['predicted_lower']['average']
        pred_upper_ci = ci.summary_data.loc['predicted_upper']['average']

        preds = ci.inferences['post_preds_means'][ci.inferences['post_preds_means'].notna()]
        test = ci.post_data['y_test']
        mape = np.mean( abs(preds - test) / test)

        result_row = {'simulated_effect': round(effect, 2), 
                      'p_value': round(ci.p_value, 2),
                      'actual': actual,
                      'predicted': predicted,
                      'abs_effect': abs_effect,
                      'pred_lower_ci': pred_lower_ci,
                      'pred_upper_ci': pred_upper_ci,
                      'abs_diff_lower': abs(predicted-pred_lower_ci),
                      'abs_diff_upper': abs(pred_upper_ci-predicted),
                      #'cumulative_target': data[test_mask].y.sum(), 
                      #'cumulative_target_simulated': data[test_mask].y_test.sum(), 
                      'mape': mape,
                      'ci_object':ci}
        
        results.append(result_row)
    
    results = np.array(results)
    return results{noformat}

*The root cause:*

We read a lot.

MySQL is not really designed for medium-large range samples. In our case, we use a fairly wide range of dates for {{order_try}} and join {{order_try_driver}}, which consists entirely of strings.
When MySQL iterate rows, the engine internally iterates through all the data in the rows of a table, since they are physically located together in segments/pages/blocks (I don't remember how in MySQL terminology) of memory, which increases the load on reading.

*As a short-term solution* - limit the range period, for example, for 1 month and execute x*months separate queries in a row.
*As a mid-term solution* -- move the {{is_optional}} column from {{order_try_driver}} to a separate table and join it.
*As a long-term solution* - move the data for drivers to a separate storage (optimize MySQL tables or use an OLAP database) and make selections from there.



I checked 2+ more the most heavy SQL’s and the issue is quite similar. Need to minimize reads by periods.

MM agents can’t filter out *Authority,* because we are working on 23 countries and Authority user persona includes tickets from all verticals. 

By changing the user persona to *Scooter Rider* while handling the ticket, we ensure that MM agents see only MM related Authority requests. Before sending a final response to the Authority - agent change the user persona back to *Authority*.

If we didn’t change the user persona to *Scooter Rider*, then *Authority* queue would be filled with both RH and MM Authority requests and agents would have to double check tickets, because RH team doesn’t change *“Authority”* to *“Rider”*.
We have previously agreed with RH teams that if they come across a MM related Authority request then it should be escalated to MM by: *Scooter Rider + Tier 1 + None*

So materializing would look like:

* Define metric.
* Run metricflow with {{--explain}} to compile the SQL.
* Use this SQL for a model to materialize.

Accordingly, the owner of the car sharing vehicles or the rental owner ( in the event Zity is only renting the assets) must comply with the following reporting obligations:

*  *Car sharing label/ authorisation granted by the city →* (ie Lyon) under transport regulations, the operator of a car sharing service such as Zity has to provide the relevant competent transport regulator (“autorité organisatrice de la mobilité” or cities) with the information or documents required to obtain or renew the car-sharing label (art. L.1231-14 of the French transport code) : information includes basic +administrative information on the operator, and data on the vehicle fleet and users+. 



* *Authorisation of public domain occupancy* (art. L.1231-17 of the French transport code) → in order to obtain the aforementioned authorisation Zity has to provide the licensing authority with details +on the vehicle fleet, environmental characteristics of the vehicles, operation of the service, measures taken to ensure compliance with parking or safety regulations etc.+

*Suggested T&C amendment from an SE local law perspective*

Regarding your suggested Global T&C amendment, my assessment is that the suggested clause 4.8 should be clarified a bit in order for the guidelines to be deemed incorporated by reference and applicable as part of the contract between the rider and Bolt under Swedish consumer law.

As a brief background, all contract terms must be presented to the consumer in a clear and easily accessible manner that is adapted to the format used (in a digital context such as the Rider T&Cs, adding links instead of just referring to a webpage is an example of such adaptation) before the consumer signs a contract, in order for the terms to be deemed enforceable against the consumer in the event of a dispute. Terms can be incorporated by reference, provided that the reference presents the content in a manner that fulfils said requirements (clear, easily accessible, etc.). To fulfil the requirement of being clear, a reference must contain information about the essentials of any additional obligations or requirements in the referred content that affects the consumer.

In light of the above, my assessment is that we should add some information about the contents of the guidelines in the suggested clause 4.8, to mitigate the risk of the guidelines being deemed unenforceable. Please see my suggestion to add a line in {color:#ff5630}red{color} below:

* *_4.8._* _To ensure a safe and reliable Bolt platform for everyone, we may take actions against you_{color:#ff5630}_, such as suspending you from using the platform for 6 months,_{color} _under our Marketplace Conduct Guidelines for Riders. By using Bolt app you confirm that you have read the Marketplace Conduct Guidelines for Riders and agree to comply with them._

To further clarify the applicability of the guidelines, I also would like to suggest adding a line to section 7.3 in the Swedish T&Cs, please see my suggestion in {color:#ff5630}red{color} below. Please note that +the suggestion relating to section 7.3. is more of a “nice to have”+ rather than a “must have” for applicability of the guidelines under Swedish law.

* *_7.3._* _We expect that you use Bolt app in good faith and be respectful of the drivers who offer their services through Bolt app._ {color:#ff5630}_In addition to any other rights we may have to take actions against you under these General Terms and Conditions and our Marketplace Guidelines for Riders,_ {color}_Bolt retains the right to close your account if you have violated the terms set out in this General Terms and Conditions or if your activities are malicious, i.e. withholding payment for the provision of the transport service, fraud, being disrespectful towards the drivers, etc. In these cases, your Bolt app account may be revoked without prior notice._

+Main agreement:+

# At the beginning information about Bolt is requested. If we wish to pursue Estonian law, then this provision can be left in.
# Changes to clause 5.4 - the reason for including right to equitable remedy is to ensure that equitable remedy can be requested even if damages as a remedy would be an adequate alternative, because normally equitable remedy is only granted if damages are not adequate remedy, which might be hard to prove. Equitable remedy allows to seek specific performance and basically stop the other party from disseminating the confidential information. So even if the right for equitable remedy exists under the Polish law (or Estonian law if we will switch the applicable law) this provision will allow the court to honour the contractual agreement between the parties and make it easier to grant equitable relief without the need to prove that parties are entitled to it. Therefore, I would suggest to insist on leaving this provision in. However, they mention that restraining orders and permanent injunctions are not available in Polish law. This might be true, but the principles of good faith and equity exist in Polish law as ‘principles of social co-existence’, so it may happen that equitable remedies might be granted to some extent, but there is no certainty. Taking that into account and also the fact that equitable remedies are more common in the UK than elsewhere, if they do not agree with our request to leave this wording in - that would not be a deal breaker.

Here is the proposed new wording: “_Co-operator undertakes to indemnify and hold NielsenIQ harmless with respect to any liability towards third parties in case any third party files any claim against NielsenIQ in relation to the use of Co-operator’s data in accordance with the Agreement infringing the copyright, patent, registered design, trade mark, design right, moral right or other intellectual property right of any third party, as well as to cover any damages incurred by NielsenIQ in that respect._”. Here is the current regulation:

{quote}§ 34.   Agreement on reimbursement of training costs
  (1) The employer and the employee may agree that the employer will incur additional costs for the training of the employee in relation to the reasonable costs incurred for the training of the employee and that the employee will work for the employer for the agreed period of time (the binding period) to reimburse these costs.

  (2) An agreement on training costs applies only if:
  A. the agreement is in writing;
  B. the agreement specifies the content of the training and the costs;
  C. the binding period does not exceed three years;
  D. the binding period is not unreasonably long having regard to the cost of the training.

  (3) The employee shall reimburse the additional costs incurred by the employer in proportion to the time remaining until the end of the commitment period if the employee terminates the employment contract before the end of the commitment period, unless the termination is due to a material breach of the employment contract by the employer.

  (4) The employee shall reimburse the additional costs incurred by the employer in proportion to the time remaining until the end of the period of engagement if the employer terminates the contract of employment before the end of the period of engagement on the grounds of a material breach of the contract of employment by the employee.

  (5) An agreement for the reimbursement of training expenses concluded with a minor or with an employer for the reimbursement of expenses incurred in the performance of a statutory training obligation shall be null and void.{quote}

# We are able to conclude such agreement, tho there are no firm limits set. This could be yearly training budget per person. This means, if the budget is 500 EUR per year, and the training is 1000 EUR, we could go and conclude the agreement. 
# Reasonable expenses is up to interpretation. Usually this means any additional cost (accomodation, transport) is included in the agreement, but not taxes and levies, if such training is subject to it. 
# I have seen that the agreements are concluded for extra-curricular trainings (like a fringe benefit) and for trainings that are required for a position (like, super-expensive training). The law states that the employer has to provide the employee with trainings that are necessary for executing their duties. This is kind-of a test - if we see that the person can do the work without the training, we don’t have to make it available, but if we decide to do so, we can conclude the agreement. If we see that this training is absolute must have and they cannot fulfil the role without it, then we should take the cost.

Hi Martyna! Thank you for your patience. Great questions!

I understand and support the drive for standartization of global processes. I will try to explain the current situation in Spain and let’s see 🙂 

*Why I think it wouldn’t be important for OPS to know about the driver issues from the 1st complaint?*

* 1 complain is not a proof of malicious behaviour, it can be accidental, or could be a false report. Historically we look at behaviour trends. 
* We have been working with a certain process logic for 2 years I’ve been with the market. For example, for _Ride did not happen_ we used to have a blocking logic that Ops approved (and they still follow this logic), where we only take action towards the driver from the 2nd report. Same for Safety in Spain - we currently follow a specific set of processes - in minor/severe cases we only issue warnings/block from 2+ report. 
* Spanish Ops prefer to not be included unless action should be taken from their side, they are pretty overwhelmed. 



*Current Ops / CS workflow* 

Our Local Ops team refuse to use Beehive due to it not having personal queues/notifications, and low volumes of escalations handled specifically by the in-house Ops team. 

Ops have an OS team who handle the Local Ops tier in Beehive, so this tier is only used for simpler issues that can be completely handled by OS Ops (i.e. activating drivers)

The current flow was set up due to request from Ops and their way of organising the workflow. So, we have 2 channels of CS escalating to Ops:

* *Local Ops tier*: handled by OS agents who are managed by Ops themselves. The tier is for simpler cases that do not require intervention from Bolt's Ops team.
* CS/Ops *Slack* channel: for cases to be handled by Ops themselves. This is the preferred method of escalation for them as CS can tag the specific person responsible for each city. 
** We have adapted the [*lost item process*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360002893034] after Joanna’s reviewal and created a specific channel for OS to escalate to in-house Ops directly. Previously we were escalating by tier 1 → tier 2 → Ops in Slack, now it’s tier 1 → Ops in Slack. Joanna offered to create the Slack channel for OS → Ops. 
*** If the item is valuable (e.g. laptop, keys, important documents), escalate the case to the local Ops team in the _#ext-majorel-bolt-rides_ channel so they will call the fleet owner

So, my idea is to basically extrapolate the Lost item escalation step to DS processes. Please let me know what you think! If you want, feel free to schedule a call to discuss this 🙂

+*Is this low risk or high risk*+ 

Provided that Bolt is covered from an insurance perspective (Tbc by Daniel) and appropriate waiver is in place then this is low risk. However, we must take into consideration that under the laws of England and Wales it is  not possible to exclude or restrict liability for death or personal injury resulting from negligence under the Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977 which states:

*Section 2: Negligence liability.*

*(1)* A person cannot by reference to any contract term or to a notice given to persons generally or to particular persons exclude or restrict his liability for death or personal injury resulting from negligence.

*(2)*In the case of other loss or damage, a person cannot so exclude or restrict his liability for negligence except in so far as the term or notice satisfies the requirement of reasonableness.

Hi Team, 

So for the completeness sharing the conclusions.

{quote}Data scrapping activity can be seen as problematic activity from legal perspective and depending on the case be qualified as e.g.: {quote}

* a breach of the terms of service (if data scrapping is explicitly prohibited in the t&c), or
* an act of unfair competition (reproducing target’s database for sake of building our own business), or
* an IP breach (database rights), or
* a criminal offence (an accessing information not intended for a person by hacking or bypassing IT software or using software to obtain such information.

{quote}Therefore, it is possible to successfully challenge potential data scraping activities and claim remedies, including damages (for loss and lost earnings). The criminal consequences cannot be fully excluded as well:{quote}

* it is difficult to estimate the actual level of risk of any consequences as: success is heavily dependent on the qualities of the target data / database, as well as the detection based on scale, frequencies, using crawlers or other automations. 
* if t&c do not clearly prohibit or done at small scale - risk low to moderate given high burden of proof.

{quote}In this case, the risk is to certain extent mitigated given that (not fully excluded though):{quote}

* we scrutinize third party service providers we engage with - from discussions with [~accountid:63a583d78a07cbd184a96e54], I understand that the provider is reliable and established on the market;
* the engagement and liability exposure is framed in the contract (please note the proposed changes which contribute thereto).
* the concerned data is not sensitive information, not related to pricing or any equivalent info.
* the practice will be limited in scale and frequency - as long as the practice does not overwhelm the target’s servers or not compromise target’s service during the data scraping process, the activity will be likely to fly under a radar.

I added the changes to [the document|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1deGEMmRzagifoHbpinMsgT2SNIqQ93LL/edit]:

* Order - please do not mention any specific market player's name and rely on the scope of the services agreed between the parties - I understand that there is already sufficient understanding between Bolt and the provider as to the scope of the agreement (the data scope, the services, the players, etc.) - based on the samples you have received and direct contracts you have had;
* 3.2 indemnification clause - the changes made are intended to ensure that the services are provided in accordance with the law and that the provider will indemnify Bolt or its directors/employees against any claims made against them in respect of services provided by the provider
* 3.3 liability clause - in general, the liability of the provider was capped up to 12 months fees (for any damage caused by the provider to Bolt), but we should exclude from this limitation any potential breach of confidentiality obligation or IP breaches - in such cases the harm to Bolt may far exceed 12 months fees. 
* 5.6 post-termination - this clause is too far reaching, in particular we cannot accept the provider’s rights to audit Bolt. Therefore, I suggested its deletion.  



Other comments / recommendations:

* Section 2.2 - I see that under section 2.2 Bolt has right to download the data. As a global approach, we advise the team not to do that for the cases where this information might be found in our servers during the court discovery process.

*Confluence*: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~247405298/pages/4545642699/Fine-tuning+a+Tesseract+Model|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~247405298/pages/4545642699/Fine-tuning+a+Tesseract+Model|smart-link] 

*Description*:

We fine-tuned a Tesseract model on 🇩🇪 *DE Drivers License*, focusing on the {{document_number}}, which posed problems and made us use *Textract*, in the first iteration:

*Results*:

Accuracy on {{document_number}} field:

* Untuned Tesseract + Google OCR + Textract ---> 91.8% *(prod)*
* Finetuned Tesseract + Google OCR + Textract --> 98.9% *(alternative 1)*
* Finetuned Tesseract + Google OCR --> 97.6% *(alternative 2)*

*Details*:

Some details about the fine-tuning process:

* Built Tesseract 5 from source files (to be tested if it's really required)
* started from the English model (for {{document_number}} it doesn't need to be German since it only contains letters and digits)
* used the bounding boxes and their labels from LJ2, for {{document_number}}  only (to train faster), in total around 500 samples
* Fine-tuned the Tesseract model
* used this fine-tuned model for {{document_number}} field only (used Tesseract 4, so that I can compare directly with the results reported on Confluence)
* using the new Tesseract model is quite easy:
* just replaced: {{cfg = "--oem 1 --psm 7 -c tessedit_char_whitelist=\"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ\" load_system_dawg false load_freq_dawg false",}}
* with: {{cfg = "--tessdata-dir /home/mardale.andrei/workspace/tesseract_train/tesstrain/data -l docnumber --oem 1 --psm 7 -c tessedit_char_whitelist=\"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ\" load_system_dawg false load_freq_dawg false"}}

Applying a fine-tuned tesseract model on a single text field has both pros and cons:

* *pros*:
*# we don't need to worry that we're going to affect other text fields than the one we target
*# the custom tesseract model will be very effective for the given font of the text field
* *cons*:
*# we might end up having specialised models for each text fields
*# there might be a danger of overfitting (since we basically fine tuned the tesseract on the desired field only)

*Next Steps:*

In the future, we might want to test with general fine-tuned models (i.e. use multiple text fields of the same document or even multiple documents of the same language), but since we don't have a good way to validate our changes on all previously trained OCR models, this should be done with care. This was just a POC to see if it's hard or not to fine-tune a model, and from my perspective, it seems quite easy:

# Building Tesseract raised no problems
# Preparing training data is straightforward, given our already labeled images (Tesseract 5 training requires input images to be one line, but in their training repo they have a script for splitting stacked lines in multiple files)
# Plugging the new model in our existing pipeline is simply a matter of updating that config which we already define at a text field level.

I added [~accountid:712020:0c8dd65b-46d5-4dc0-b5bd-76209c1e8048] to the ticket (Rentals). In Switzerland the new data protection act will be effective *in September* (see provided overview: July). To summarise before I close the ticket:

1.) Right now we are offering scooters in two cities (Winterthur, Zürich)

2.) *No immediate for a DPO (neither for local entity nor bolt operations)* (no need but it would be voluntary to skip the prior consolidation with the local DPA (similar mechanic like Art 36 GDPR). DPO team also got access to the online-platform to register a DPO if needed (No requirement for the DPO to be located in Switzerland. 

3.) *No immediate to name a local representative (Sec 14 nDSG):* This is necessary for foreign controllers to appoint a representative in Switzerland if they process the personal data of persons in Switzerland and the data processing meets the following requirements:

* The processing is related to the offer of goods and services or the observation of the behavior of individuals in Switzerland. ✅ 
* It is a case of large-scale processing. ✅ 
* The processing is carried out on a regular basis. ✅ 
* The processing involves a {color:#ff5630}*high risk to the personality rights of the data subjects.*{color}❌ 

*more info on the "high risk"*

* The used term in  is similar to the one used in Sec 22 nDSG (Talking about DPIA)
_”Sec 22 (1) If processing is likely to result in a high risk to the data subject's personality or fundamental rights, the controller shall carry out a data protection impact assessment beforehand. If several similar processing procedures are planned, a joint assessment may be carried out._
^_(2)_^ _The existence of a high risk, in particular when using new technologies, depends on the nature, extent, circumstances and purpose of the processing. A high risk arises in particular:_
_a. in the case of the large-scale processing of sensitive personal data;_
_b. if public areas are systematically monitored on a large scale.”_

*If the controller discovers that rentals will process data of Swiss data subjects and that would require a DPIA (unter GDPR/ or Swiss nDSG), we kindly recommend that you inform the DPO team. We already cleared with Merve that the Swiss team is not only a post box, so we can name them as local representative publish the name and the address of the representative pretty quick (Contact details of the Swiss entity are already on the website but for more transparency we could add it in the privacy notice)*{color:#ff5630} *(Duties and liabilities of the representatives in the summary below)*{color} [~accountid:712020:0c8dd65b-46d5-4dc0-b5bd-76209c1e8048] if you are dealing with a DPIA for processing activities scooter (also in switzerland) please be aware of that. 

4.) *Privacy Notice: necessary adaption* of the privacy notice *(specify all recipient countries)* are listed in the Privacy Notice requirements (shared with Privacy legal: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1w-J7OTcbc1pBjGj496gAKtdU_w_oGMiKbYFPq5uiloc/edit#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1w-J7OTcbc1pBjGj496gAKtdU_w_oGMiKbYFPq5uiloc/edit#gid=0|smart-link] )

5.){color:#ff5630} *Reminder:* {color}

* As already in the existing DPA, but in contrast to the GDPR, it is not the company that is liable for violations of the nDSG, but the natural person within the company responsible for the violation (CEO, person responsible for the organization). The liability of managers is clarified with the reference to Art. 6 VStrR in Art. 64 nDSG. This is the only way to ensure that persons in management positions are liable for the violations and not the freshly hired employee.
* Exceptionally, according to Art. 64 para. 2 nDSG, companies can also be held directly liable. if a fine of no more than *CHF 50,000.00* comes into consideration and the investigation of the person liable to prosecution according to Art. 6 VStrR appears disproportionate.

Let me answer at least a few of those questions - I feel there’s some kind of misunderstanding. There’s no device nor browser information stored anywhere in our process, as you can read in the initial report:

{quote}
*Specify the types of personal data that will be processed or transferred as part of your project.*

every URLs visited and interacted (number of clicks, scrolls and keystrokes - just count, not what was typed), with timestamp{quote}

We collect only that set of data - For user identification, we prompt them with a single input field, and that’s the way we tell them apart. We don’t store any extra browser or device information. 

When it comes to cookies - the extension has nothing to do with cookies itself - it’s not trying to read 3rd party cookies, doesn’t steal them from visited pages nor uses them for its own purposes. 

But maybe there’s some sort of misunderstanding - it’s not really a technology I could really use directly to collect data, cookies are a way (pretty ancient) to store data on a user’s computer. So if you’re asking if we’re storing something on a computer then yes, not as a cookie but the whole extension is downloaded and stored on the computer, It’s not our choice, that’s how all extensions work.

Huge companies are also using cookies to identify users and track their behaviors. They track every activity anyway, unwillingly to the users, from different domains, and with cookies it’s easier for them to glue one puzzle piece to another. 
We do it completely differently - users’ browsers share everything with us willingly. And since the extension is running on users' computers, this ‘glue’ part is not a challenge - just everything that we collect here is from one user.

# _Usually the registration of the NGO at the Ministry of Justice is delayed for months, which could be 8-9 months (our experience) or even more (from public complaints), or sometimes refused (from public complaints, mainly when political issues are involved). We have observed very quick registration cases with certain support letters (just 1.5 months, our experience), as well._ 
_Therefore, we have suggested obtaining recommendation/support letters from the relevant government agency while applying for the registration._ 

# _The most suitable organizational legal form for your desired scope would be Association (for example, “Association of passenger transport companies”). Per our legislation, an Association is a non-profit organization formed of commercial legal entities, united based on common interests, equality of participants (members) and on voluntary basis._
 
_Any person can be appointed as head of the Association with the consent of other participants, so your intention to appoint a representative of Bolt as the head of the Association is possible, provided that other members do not object. Since the head is appointed at the time of registration, we do not think that appointment of Bolt representative will be an issue. Please also note that in case if founder of Association is a foreign legal person, the deputy head of Association must be a citizen of the Republic of Azerbaijan._
 
_As an example, we can mention the following commercial associations currently operating in Azerbaijan:_
 
## _Azerbaijan Construction Manufacturers Association;_
## _Pomegranate Production and Export Association of Azerbaijan;_
## _Azerbaijan jewelers’ association etc._
#  
_We have extensive experience in handling registration and ongoing legal scope of NGO’s, Associations included. That all being said, please be mindful that the registration of NGOs is under supervision of the Ministry of Justice, which applies a rather conservative approach and scrutinizes each application. In practice, there is a need for a powerful local partner and an unofficial “green light” from the Ministry prior to application process. In the absence of such, they tend to delay the process and come up with ridiculous arguments in order to reject registration._

_This is a complicated processs and as I mentioned before we cannot guarantee successful registration, but if you would still want to proceed our fixed fee will be USD 4500. The anticipated timeline is 3-4 months._

Hey Piotr,

There are two types of cookies - 1st parties and 3rd parties. 3rd parties are used for tracking behaviour and profiling, ads. 1st parties cookies are used for different purposes, even when you log-in in the web app or page, it creates cookies to remember you during the session. 



The data collected through cookies can be different and in this case (number of clicks, scrolls and keystrokes) are collected from cookies. User installs the extension that can track this set of data, Bolt has access to this data because browser sends this data to us. That’s how cookies work. In our case it’s not 3rd parties cookies that can track their behaviour and be used for the ads, it’s 1st parties cookies that are still collected from the user’s browser for our purpose.

Since these are cookies or even if it’s no cookies, agents should give explicit consent for access to browser’s information according to ePrivacy Directive: ‘the use of electronic communications networks *to store information or to gain access to information stored in the terminal equipment of a subscriber or user is only allowed on condition that the subscriber or user* *is offered the right to refuse such processing by the data controller.' i.e., consent.*

That’s why we need to proceed with drafting the consent for them and think of how we will send this and collect this consent from agents for gain access or store (number of clicks, scrolls and keystrokes) info on their equipment. The further processing is covered by the GDPR and our legitimate interest.
