The requirement to get the consent applies not only to cookies in question, but for any information that we access from user’s equipment. Directive says ‘*to store information or to* +*gain access to*+ +*_information_*+ +*stored in the terminal equipment of a subscriber or user*+ *is only allowed on condition that the subscriber or user* *is offered the right to refuse such processing by the data controller.' i.e., consent.*

In our case, we get access to the info from agent’s compute/browser to track and analyse this info, it means that requirement above applies and we need to ask for their consent to get access to this info before we ask them to install the extension.

You can send this consent (I will prepare today), wait for their consent, and provide instructions only to those that have agreed.

*Regarding stolen orders* (the order has been already taken by someone else): it’s a complicated issue and as I see it we can distinguish three types of cases, the proposition of the procedure is the following: 

* In the order was 1 courier who arrived at the restaurant (we assume that the provider is at fault):
** Call the restaurant 2 times and ask to reprepare the order (*without compensation*)
** If they agree, we inform all the parties about the delay and no further action needed
** If they don’t agree or don’t pick up the phone, we fail the order with the provider at fault
* In the order, there were 2 couriers and it’s clear the 1st courier has taken the order and re-dispatched themselves right after (the 1st courier is at fault):
** Call the restaurant 2 times and ask them to reprepare the order (*with compensation*)
** If they agree, we inform all the parties about the delay and compensate the provider (and probably the courier)
** If they don’t agree or don’t pick up the phone, we fail the order with Bolt at fault
** Blocking tool for the 1st courier + deduction (up to 50 pln - e.g. we treat it as a “stolen order” case - this is our internal agreement confirmed with legal)
* There were several couriers, it’s impossible to assess who was at fault:
** Same as above but we don’t block anyone  

The proposition is not final - it’s just an idea (and for now, I don’t have exact data).

Hi, [~accountid:61e9466c5fcc370068849a81]! I have reviewed the CDA (NDA) and there are some concerns regarding its provisions. I am not sure how much negotiation power we have, but if we do have some, then we need to address these issues: 

# This is a unilateral NDA where all the obligations are borne by Bolt alone. WIll we share any confidential information with them? If yes, then we need to sign a mutual NDA. Information about our template can be found [+here+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3434252224/Non-Disclosure+Agreement+NDA+Self+Service].
# There is no clause that allows us to share confidential information within our group. Although the clause 1.4 is quite wide, it does not mention employees of other group companies. This is something that would be nice to have, but if we know that we will share any information between several entities then we need to ensure that this is permitted under the NDA.
# Term of the NDA in clause 1.8: it is an NDA that lasts indefinitely and can be terminated only by giving 6+ months prior notice. This is unusual, but not critical. Our standard wording in this respect is “This Agreement automatically will terminate upon the earlier of (i) termination of all written agreements between the parties or their Affiliates regarding the Relationship, or (ii) if no agreements are executed, termination of discussions between the parties or their Affiliates regarding the Relationship or delivery of written notice terminating this Agreement;“. I suggest proposing something similar or at least shorten the termination notice to 30 days. 
# Penalties in clause 1.9: there is a contractual penalty for breach of confidentiality obligations in the sum of 1 mln CZK (approximately 41 500 EUR). We should not agree to this clause, because they will be able to claim penalties even when the breach will not cause any harm to them.

Please note that in order to send this NDA for signing all relevant fields need to be completed beforehand. Also, the NDA requires a qualified electronic signature, therefore it should be signed using Dokobit.

Feel free to reach out if you have any questions.

I’m not saying that it’s bad if we send only issue we are sure of to GPT, it might be good. If any, we can prompt GPT to ask for details until we are certain of the issue. On the other hand, we’d need to make comparative performance on the model for that (AB test?).

What I’d like to discuss / ask is where “80%” comes from, how it’s computed and what is the impact on coverage?

Usually we rely on “accuracy” or “precision” objective. Models basically return a vector of probabilities for each issues. So one pred can be a vector {{[0.02, 0.3, 0.005, 0.43, ...]}} with sum to 1. These are long vectors (like few hundreds of elements), so in that context, 30% of probability for top issue might already be plenty. Usually, we auto select probability threshold to have an accuracy of 0.8. That is not to say that the probability itself is 80%, and actually most often it is much less than that.

My main message here is:

* top 1 issue, probably not a bad idea for GPT
** but needs to be confirmed / tested
* in general, attention how threshold is implemented. Blunt 80% on top issue probability will most probably reduce coverage (prop. of cases for with issue is returned given criteria) drastically
** DS endpoint can probably be adapted to return useful input there

About partition keys filtering, detailed answer from dbt:

[https://getdbt.slack.com/archives/C02CCBBBR1D/p1693414537100759?thread_ts=1693377971.986879&cid=C02CCBBBR1D|https://getdbt.slack.com/archives/C02CCBBBR1D/p1693414537100759?thread_ts=1693377971.986879&cid=C02CCBBBR1D|smart-link] 

Our partition support needs work.We have three layers of partition support at the moment, but none of them is quite right so we need to work on it.

# Direct filter on a partition column used as a dimension. If you put this in the metric filter definition it may produce a pruned query, but this depends on how the engine implements pushdown.
# Start time and end time query parameters - at query time you can specify start and end time, and if your agg_time_dimension is the partition column we should push those down and trigger partition pruning
# Partition joins - if you specify a dimension as a partition, we'll use it in the join condition if you link it to another partition dimension with the same name. Except I don't think this works correctly at the moment.

In the future we'd like to consolidate all of this into two pieces:

# Partition dimension designation for better automation on partition pruning in filters and joins (e.g., if you have a "load time" partition you can configure that to automatically get a filter based on metric_time filter conditions).
# Filter pushdown to ensure partition filters trigger pruning regardless of engine. This is a work in progress. See [https://github.com/dbt-labs/metricflow/issues/747|https://github.com/dbt-labs/metricflow/issues/747|smart-link]

Hey [~accountid:61824756892c420072e63853], thank you for your explanations.

There is no part in our Rider T&Cs that  describes how the categories have been ordered since there is no requirement to do so. However, as of February 2024 we will need to explain it in our T&Cs to some extent due to the new EU Regulation entering into force.

But as to your main question, me and [~accountid:626fb920f42962006fde4c04] have conducted some research on reordering the categories in Rider app based on the notion that the rider is a ‘tourist’, and we found out that reordering the categories based on *_rider’s nationality, place of residence or place of establishment_* is not allowed under the EU laws.

Here is what we believe you could think of to still proceed with the plan to some extent (if commercially feasible):

# Define a rider group(s) that that achieves a similar effect, however is not based on nationality, place of residence or place of establishment;
# Collect explicit user consent (e.g. a "Welcome to Croatia" card with an "agree" or an "X" button for travelling users to opt in to 'tourist offers', re-ordering, language preferences etc.); OR
# Proceed with the feature with an "acknowledged risk" that it may breach this Regulation. Arguments in favour of this position are that while Bolt technically may be in breach, the change is low-profile with an arguably low risk of detection, re-ordering is unlikely to cause consumers significant harm, the feature applies to _all_ visitors (not one country or nationality specifically) and Recital 9 notes that services in the field of transport are excluded from the Regulation (though this could open a whole other can of worms about Bolt's agency business model classification).

While considering the third option, please also note that as of February 2024 we will be required to disclose that we are engaging in this practice in our T&Cs. This would make the practice even more visible for the riders and authorities.

Let me know if you have any questions.

Julia

Example with 1 dimension model and 2 fact models, metrics from each fact table. 

{noformat}---
semantic_models:
  - name: rides_orders
    defaults:
      agg_time_dimension: created_date_local
    description: Rides orders fact table.
    model: ref('etl_fact_rides_orders')
    # Entities. These usually corespond to keys in the table.
    entities:
      - name: order_key
        type: primary
      - name: city_id
        type: foreign
        expr: city_id
    # Measures. These are the aggregations on the columns in the table.
    measures:
      - name: rides_orders_created
        expr: 1
        agg: sum
    # Dimensions. Either categorical or time.
    dimensions:
      - name: created_date
        type: time
        type_params:
          time_granularity: day
      - name: created_date_local
        type: time
        type_params:
          time_granularity: day
      - name: order_id
        type: categorical
      - name: has_campaign_code
        type: categorical
        expr: case when campaign_code is null then 0 else 1 end
      - name: created_hour_local
        type: categorical

  - name: rides_order_tries
    defaults:
      agg_time_dimension: created_date_local
    description: Rides order tries fact table.
    model: ref('etl_fact_rides_order_tries')
    # Entities. These usually corespond to keys in the table.
    entities:
      - name: order_try_key
        type: primary
      - name: city_id
        type: foreign
        expr: city_id
    # Measures. These are the aggregations on the columns in the table.
    measures:
      - name: rides_order_tries_created
        expr: 1
        agg: sum
    # Dimensions. Either categorical or time.
    dimensions:
      - name: created_date
        type: time
        type_params:
          time_granularity: day
      - name: created_date_local
        type: time
        type_params:
          time_granularity: day
      - name: created_hour_local
        type: categorical

  - name: admin_system_city
    description: City dimension
    model: ref('stg_ng_public__admin_system_city')
    # Entities. These usually corespond to keys in the table.
    entities:
      - name: city_id
        type: primary
    # Measures. These are the aggregations on the columns in the table.

    # Dimensions. Either categorical or time.
    dimensions:
      - name: city_name
        type: categorical
{noformat}

Notice that city_id is entity and it is no longer in the dimensions section in any of the models.

{noformat}SELECT
  COALESCE(subq_7.city_id, subq_13.city_id, subq_19.city_id) AS city_id

  FROM (

    FROM `dbt_silja_mardla_spark`.`etl_fact_rides_orders` rides_orders_src_2
    WHERE created_date_local BETWEEN '2023-08-28' AND '2023-08-29'

I won’t be able to tell you now the exact moment when this rule appeared, but as mentioned previously, it is related to collecting data about the driver’s behavior where it is not done automatically by the BQS.

The escalation to the Local OPS does not necessarily mean that the driver needs to be blocked. Markets, where the BQS is not live, have their own market-specific workflows for handling driver behavior requests. Looking forward to your reply!

# Why we had Stockholm rather than Gothenburg in the enrolment for the driver?

# We are using 7 days benchmark for the driver to look into driver's activity. If in past 7 days (from current date), the driver did not have any activity, registration city will be tagged to that particular driver. That is the reason we had Stockholm (Registration City) instead Gothenburg (Activity City).

# Why i was unable to create this scenario again?

# The reason is, we are having date filter in etl to check the past 7 days from current date and also adding 14 days (which will not have an impact if we are looking for current date but will change the scenario if we are looking for previous dates like our scenario 2023-08-21).

In general there are two places that need to be cleaned and updated when changing versions:

* virtual environment (dbt-env)
* dbt clean + dbt deps

Each cirtual environment will run on the version of Python that was active when the virtual environment was started/called/created.



Deactivating a virtual environment

{noformat}deactivate{noformat}

Creating a new virtual environment called dbt-env

{noformat}python -m venv dbt-env{noformat}

Removing a virtual environment (i.e. delete the file called dbt-env)

{noformat}rm -rfd dbt-env{noformat}

Activating a virtual environement

{noformat}source ./dbt-env/bin/activate{noformat}



The step by step list of actions from Pawel

{noformat}pyenv install 3.9
cd /path/to/dbt/repository
pyenv local 3.9
rm -rfd dbt-env
python -m venv dbt-env
source ./dbt-env/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install dbt-metrics-converter{noformat}

It does not matter which entity is issuing the promo code itself or where the rider is based.

*Investigation results*

It looks like the GoogleMapsSDK has an internal problem with calculating texture coordinates for markers.

Here is an example of a correct drawing call for no parking area icon

!Screenshot 2023-08-31 at 14.22.11.png|width=33.333333333333336%!

with texture coordinates 

!Screenshot 2023-08-31 at 14.22.21.png|width=510,height=143!

And here is the same area of the city and the marker, but texture coordinates are calculated incorrectly


!Screenshot 2023-08-31 at 14.18.54.png|width=358,height=215!

!Screenshot 2023-08-31 at 14.19.29.png|width=50%!

Perhaps this is due to the large number of markers, which, in addition, has recently been further increased by adding markers for tiles of city areas.

The problem arises if there is a lot of movement on the map (for example, zooming in and out), which causes the markers to constantly redraw. And it disappears if you move out the problem area from the rendering viewport and return it again (by moving the map). What exactly happens inside the library, we cannot say, since we do not have access to the source code. Perhaps this is a resource leak, rounding errors, or errors in the optimization algorithm.

Updating the library to the latest version does not solve the problem.


*Potential solutions*

* reduce the number of markers and the frequency of their redrawing
* use tile engine to draw cityzones (cityzone markers will be able to move to tiles as well)
* create a sample application with a similar problem to open an issue in google issue tracker

Hey. This is quite straightforward. We use Greenhouse as a platform to manage our candidates for internal positions. This entails creating flows for each employee, such as submitting a CV (we collect them via our website - Careers, via Linkedin or other job posting sites), which gets reviewed by someone at Bolt on the Greenhouse platform, after which we can send an assessment or set up interviews etc. 
The assessment mentioned can take many forms, from a simple presentation in powerpoint, to a set of questions in excel or a coding task. In this case, the test is a psychometric evaluation provided by Thrive - they have scientifically developed method to test a candidate's ability to identify patterns, math skills, logical thinking. The candidate’s answers are anonymised (we cannot see what they answered to what question) but we can see how they performed on a scale from 1 to 100 % vs other people in the same position who took the test. For example, an Operations Specialist could rank in the top 10% of the people with that position who took the test.

Can you provide more context about why you need to link self-help articles in replies to users? The 2 articles you linked are quite short, so the information could be sent to the user in a message instead 💭

We researched this a while ago and found that the average replies per ticket are higher for tickets where a self-help article was linked. There are 2 possible reasons for this:

* The self-help article was linked to replace a part of the reply, and the user had to follow up to clarify the previous reply.
* The user needed more clarifications on their request as it was not answered by the self-help article.

We also found that only around 30% of people opened the link on average.

Based on this, and because we currently cannot always provide an article in the same language, I would advise against sending any articles and instead provide the information directly in the ticket.

I'm aware that we provide Russian language support to users in Latvia, but the task of translating all articles into Russian is a large one and is not something we have the capacity to do at the moment, so we’re planning to look into it in the future.

We do have section 4 in our standard General Terms: Data processing agreement, which states that both Parties remain separate data controllers (see bilingual version [here|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/2aDCZWENCfByCjLQWy3Sy9/6b85b4097a1380ce2a8bdd000391bbcd/PL_-_Ogo__lne_warunki_Bolt_Business__obowia__zuja___od_1.03.2023_r._.docx.pdf]). 

In Bolt Business contracts, Bolt determines the means and purposes of processing personal data to provide the platform and fulfil the agreement and is deemed as the controller and not the processor. As a controller Bolt determines the means and purposes for processing the data in order to provide the service (Bolt Business to the Customer). Bolt is the one registering and administering the users, providing the platform and providing the opportunity for Users to make use of Bolt Business in the limits set by Customers.

I believe that the customer is of opinion that we have processor relationship here, and not controller-to-controller - and this is the reason behind their request.

Hey again!I am in the middle of migrating to MetricFlow (as you probably have guessed by the number of questions and comments I've been posting).
There is one more thing that I want to point out regarding the deprecation of {{metrics.calculate}} and the workaround with MetricFlow query with {{--explain}}.The main reason why we love the metrics is that they basically provide column by column data lineage for our data marts.
My data lineage graph used to be

{noformat}source1 -> fact_table1 -> metric1, metric2, metric3 -> data_mart
source2 -> fact_table2 -> metric4, metric5          -> data_mart{noformat}

where data_mart is the same table and I can see it depends on 5 metrics that in turn depend on 2 fact tables.After migration I just have broken lineage:

{noformat}source1 -> fact_table1 -> metric1, metric2, metric3 (no downstream dependencies)
source2 -> fact_table2 -> metric4, metric5          (no downstream dependencies)

(no upstream dependencies) -> data_mart{noformat}

So... uh... can you at least come up with a way to (manually) add some comments into the data_mart model so that it would know that it depends on these specific metrics?I hope you were aware of this before my post. And I also hope that this can be fixed, even if the fix is somewhat ugly.
I did not realise before that the lineage will be broken and I am currently very disappointed...PS: I am otherwise very happy about the positive things that MetricFlow brings to table! (edited)

Hi! I did a [small deepdive on the data requests|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1k5Txq1i9fLZL9Z3zpicBQ9ToqF8jEFNsrsjQrTON21g/] we have received over the past 3 months. I thought that this could potentially aid in giving more insight for these potential guidelines, so I am sharing here as well. The deepdive outlines what were the most common types of requests and the specific data that was asked for.

Just for clarity:

* the date is the exact day when the _request for data_ was made, rather than when ticket was raised
* the type of request investigates what was the _most_ specific request. So for example, if the client says ‘I want *all my data* including *all reviews from drivers*’ then I put it down as a request for driver reviews - I was trying to go after the most specific requests mentioned only, as they can give us insight into what users are (potentially) targeting
* I also included if the request for data comes from a complaint regarding a specific ride, or if the requests are seemingly not connected to experiences with the platform.

From the results it is visible that we receive a wide range of requests for very specific points of data, which in most cases are not part of the GDPR export. I hope that this data can help at least a little in investigating and devising potential guidelines.

Copy-paste of the section for better persistence

h2. Commission in Aggregated Invoice

There are different ways to associate commission to the aggregated invoice, with different behaviors in case of delays on the side of Bolt.

h3. Option 1: Invoice has all Commissions not yet Invoiced (last month + previous)

# Commission Record is initially saved *without* invoice_external_id
# Provider Invoice Task has no dependencies: always runs on a fixed date (e.g. 5th of Month)
# Provider Invoice Task Processor queries all Commission Records *without invoice external id*
# Provider Invoice Task Processor updates invoice_external_id on Records, indicating they’ve been processed
# Invoice has a single row for all commissions

h3. Option 1b

# Invoice has one row per month

h3. Option 2: Invoice has all Commissions from orders for last month

# Commission Record is initially saved *with invoice_external_id (with month encoded in ID)*
# Provider Invoice Task *is dependent* on commission record tasks
# Provider Invoice Task queries all Commission Records with this invoice’s *invoice_external_id*
# Records don’t need to be updated after processing

h3. Option 2 variant B

The same as above, but use *action_timestamp* for association of commissions to their month & monthly invoice.

Article 1 of the Royal Decree 933/2021, of 26 October says: _the purpose of this Royal Decree is to regulate the documentary registration and information obligations provided for in the regulations for the protection of public safety for natural or legal persons who carry out, professionally or otherwise, activities of accommodation or_ +_rental of motor vehicles without drivers._+

Article 2 defines the activities of renting motor vehicles without a driver as follows: _activities carried out for the purpose of facilitating their use by a third party, for a specific period of time, and in exchange for compensation, consideration or a certain price. In any case, the following activities are included in this definition:_
_(a) Those carried out by undertakings expressly engaged in the hire of vehicles._
_[...]._
_c) The activity of digital platforms dedicated, for payment or free of charge, to intermediation in these activities via the Internet, whether or not they provide the underlying service that is the object of mediation, provided that they offer services in Spain._



In light of the above article, I am inclined to think that both Zity and Bolt may be subject to this Royal Decree and have to comply with the obligations set out in the Decree, which are as follows:



+_Article 5. Documentary registration obligations._+ 

_1. Data subjects shall keep a computer register containing the data listed in Annexes I and II, depending on the activity they carry out, including, where appropriate, the data of persons under fourteen years of age._ 

_2. The data subjects shall register and keep those data on their users, included in Annexes I and II, which they obtain in the exercise of their activity, under such terms as may be determined._ 

_3. The data in the computer register shall be kept for a period of three years from the end of the contracted service or provision._ 

_4. Obligated entities that carry out accommodation activities in a non-professional manner shall be exempt from the obligations of documentary registration and data retention provided for in this Article, and shall only be subject to the reporting obligations provided for in the following Article._

+_Article 6. Reporting obligations._+

_1. Prior to the commencement of the activity and in accordance with the procedure to be established, the regulated entities shall communicate to the competent authorities the data referred to in Annex I, section A) or B), subsections 1 and 2, or in Annex II, subsection 1, depending on the activity in question. A change in any of the above information shall give rise to a new reporting obligation._

_2. Compliance with the obligation provided for in the preceding paragraph must be must be carried out within ten days of the completion of the administrative formalities required in each case for the administrative formalities required in each case for the development of the activity and, in any case, prior to the actual in any case, prior to the effective exercise of the activity._

_3. In addition, the regulated entities shall transmit to the competent authorities the data relating to the exercise of their activity and, in any event, prior to the effective exercise thereof. the competent authorities the information relating to the exercise of their activity included in subparagraphs 3 and 4 of Annex I (A) or (B), or in Annex II (2), (3), (4) and (5), depending on the activity in question. activity concerned._

_This notification shall be made immediately, and in any case within a period not exceeding 24 hours, respectively, to 24 hours, respectively, from the following points in time:_
_a) On making the reservation or formalisation of the contract or, where applicable, its cancellation._
_b) At the start of the contracted services._

_4. The communications provided for in this article shall be made by telematic procedures. Exempt from this are those obliged parties who carry out accommodation activities in a non-professional manner, who activities in a non-professional manner, who may carry them out by non-telematic means, by the procedure to be determined._

Please note also that the Royal Decree says that the process for compliance with the reporting obligations will be established, I assume by an implementing regulation. However, I am not sure whether this regulation has already been approved. So far I have not found any complementary regulations to this Royal Decree.

Regarding the options presented by Guillermo:

# *Online intermediation services provider*. I am not sure that this is a valid argument for excluding Zity's obligation under this Royal Decree. Note that the enumeration of obliged parties in Article 2 does not seem to exclude the obligation of one of them if another is obliged or is fulfilling its obligation. I believe that the legislator did not foresee a case such as the one at hand, so it is difficult to deduce from the law an answer to this case.
# *Reseller business model.* How would this model work in practice - does Zity sell car sharing services to Bolt, bill Bolt, and then Bolt resells these services to users? In this case, I think we could argue that Zity is providing the services to Bolt so it only has to collect Bolt's data, although it seems to me to be a bit on the edge. But again, this is not something the legislator had in mind when drafting this law so the answer cannot be easily inferred from the text of the law.

[~accountid:61cc1c959ee70a00680edd89] - Unfortunately, I cannot find better arguments for not sharing with Zity the data set out in the Royal Decree. If you would like me to seek external or specialist advice, please let me know.

Thank you very much.

Copy-pasting the message from Vishal to me regarding Launch Plan:

{quote}Hey, we do not have an agreed template on it as of today. Maybe in future we can create one.But for this, I can think of following sections on top of my head -

Introduction - what the document is about and how and what will it help a reader to infer

Strategy - the details on strategy you are going with for the launch. For example you may go country by country for a launch. In our case since it is for a specific partner in a specific country we need a different one. Maybe we can divide it simply in phases - for example in phase 1 we will launch intermediate model for non business customers, in phase 2 we will launch intermediate and resale models etc. Or another strategy you can have is launch all business models but without extra fees or discount and in Phase 2 have support for extra fees and discount and in Phase 3 support for refunds and fines. It totally depend on how you want to move ahead together as a team in steps which are small yet meaningful and give you enough time and space to look back and fix things

Checklist - A set of checklist (if you have phases then each phase may have its own checklist) i.e. a set of things that need to be in place before you launch. For example approval for invoices from legal etc. The checklist can have both functional and technical items in it.

Tracker - Kind of a table or matrix that lists the progress with ETA of launch itself. For example this table (country wise launch). It is good to have corresponding JIRA tickets here (launch/roll out tickets but not the implementation tickets)

Risks - anything you wish to highlight for stakeholders and management they need to be aware about i.e. things that can go wrong or what can happen if something goes wrong

Rollback Strategy - what all needs to be done if we need to roll back if something goes terribly wrong and when should a rollback be triggered

Appendix - related documents you wish to attach to help a reader dig deeper

Open Questions (Optional)

Hey [~accountid:61c450c9e67ea2006b2caf9e],

Thank you for your understanding. Please see my thoughts on your questions below:

 1. As I mentioned we currently have city-level limits active in all markets. And we don’t show what the current limit is (in the app nor T&Cs). If I remember correctly in the T&Cs there’s clause stating that we can disable cash-rides for you but we don’t specify the exact limit. My proposal is to continue doing it but instead of city level we would have the limits defined on a driver-level instead.
*I did not locate such clause in our Driver T&Cs and this is exactly what I meant in my third question - we need to have a legal ground to do this under our current Driver T&Cs. At the same time, having this wording in our T&Cs does not release us from the requirement of letting the drivers know about what would happen if they did something. Hence, the drivers need to know the cash-blocking limits.*

[~accountid:6052891645a3bb006808f764] do you see any issues with disabling cash payments for certain drivers under payment laws? I am not aware of anything but maybe you are.

2. Yes we’re monitoring historical behaviour of the driver e.g. how long the driver has been driving with us, what’s his/hers debt repayment rate, how likely it is the driver churns etc. All the metrics contributing to the model can be seen here - [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4447076489/Driver+Credit+Score|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4447076489/Driver+Credit+Score|smart-link]

*This one is quite problematic from reclassification perspective - we can’t impose limitations on drivers based on their behaviour, this would signal employment relationship with the driver. Nevertheless, I actually think that setting the limits based on Driver Credit Score is most likely acceptable and defendable since we are not on the market to incur debt on behalf of the drivers. However, some of the metrics that we would like to include in the Credit Score are not related to the credit rating in my opinion, for example, acceptance rate, cash acceptance rate, activity rate, churn probability score. Can we filter some metrics out of the equation?*

[~accountid:6052891645a3bb006808f764] do you see any finreg or other issues with calling it Credit Score? Can it be implied that we are providing credit to the driver or anything similar if we call it this way?

3. Maybe you’ve misunderstood the concept of blocking vs cash-blocking? In case of blocking we won’t allow the drivers to take any rides. But in terms of cash-blocking we disable cash rides for them only (they can still accept & complete in-app rides). As I brought up above we have this currently live & drivers are getting cash-blocked every day/hour as we speak (due to negative balance/debt they have) but the limits are set on the city level currently & they have no visibility what the current thresholds for this are (they can only guess after they get cash-blocked)

*I think I actually got it, just expressed it in a weird way* 🙂  *It is true that cash-blocking is not the same as blocking but there needs to be a legal ground for us to do cash-blocks (as noted in section 1). To clarify, drivers need to know that we will limit their ability to take cash rides if they incur too much debt. We don’t currently have anything on this in our Driver T&Cs. The fact that we don’t have it but are still blocking drivers, does not mean we are compliant* 🙂 

Summing up the above:

* let me know if you agree with my assessment
* need to understand whether there are any markets where we can’t do that from payments laws perspective (cc [~accountid:6052891645a3bb006808f764] the same question as raised above)
* if you agree with my assessment, then we need to update T&Cs with i) legal ground for performing cash-blocks and ii) criteria of credit score that we assess for setting the limits
* we need to have something in the product for driver that would let him/her know what is his / her current threshold if it will be individual and based on a Credit Score
* [~accountid:6052891645a3bb006808f764] to confirm if calling the feature a Credit Score is fine considering our regulatory setup

Thank you, and let’s discuss if unclear.

Julia

Hi [~accountid:641d70192cee496759ec78f0], 

The police seem to refer to the Act (2014:1020) on accounting centers and ordering centers for taxi traffic. Section 24, as references by the police, only refers to the obligation of such accounting centres or ordering centres to provide information to the Tax Authority which such centres are obliged to store pursuant to the Act. The mentioned Act includes a definition of an ordering centre: “_an order center refers to a business that consists of receiving orders and payments and distributing driving assignments between holders of taxi traffic permits_”. This is exactly what Bolt does so Bolt is considered the ordering centre. 

However, the sections references by the police do not provide the obligation to provide information to anyone else but the Tax Authority. There is an obligations to store certain data which is described in the aforementioned Act and the Taxi Traffic Act (2012:211). 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Hi [~accountid:5d8df399c7d4e30dc2836580] 

Please find *_attached_* our WIP Refund guidelines for the UK.

I’ll need to get in a call with you/your team this month to go over any common refund scenarios I haven’t captured here and to get your feedback on what you may need further from the doc so this is a useful point of reference for all moving forward. 

Once we have the internal guidelines finalised between our teams, legal can then get working on a public facing Refunds Policy, which our CS agents can then refer to for any disputes arising. 

With specific reference to your questions raised, I’ve now reviewed and answers are below: 

*Questions:*

* Does Bolt have an obligation to refund the passenger if they complain about the trip being shorter?
** *Answer: In short, no Bolt is not legally obligated to give a refund here.* Bolt provides passengers with an estimated fare, and the passenger agrees to this at the start of the journey before getting into the vehicle (contract is formed), they have consented to pay for the full journey (at the estimated rate) and therefore are not entitled to a refund if they simply exit the vehicle earlier. 
** Unless express agreement is provided to change the fare between the parties involved (Passenger >Driver >Bolt) this wont give rise to a refund. So for example, if there is a situation where the passenger and driver agree to cut the journey shorter, and they ensure this is changed within the App (a revised agreement on the fare), but the passenger still get charged the full fare, then we only need to refund the passenger the difference in fare amounts between the agreed fare and the revised fare (this is then reflected on what the driver gets paid).
** It is up to Bolt whether it provides a gesture of goodwill (not a refund) paying the difference in amounts, but this ultimately remains a business decision and can be assessed on a case by case basis on whether Bolt wants to absorb this cost. 
* Does Bolt have an obligation to pay the driver the fare that was shown to him on acceptance?
** Answer: Yes the driver should be paid the fare shown to him on acceptance if they complete this journey in line with what they have agreed with Bolt. Unless further agreement changed this amount (in line with the above) or the trip didn't occur at all. 
** If Bolt moves to an agency model, this process will need to be revised and it’s presently being considered with the new guidelines (applicable to the Principal model atm). 
** It is worth noting, that drivers abusing this process can fall fowl of our fraud policy so it’s worth flagging when/if this becomes problematic with your teams. 

Many thanks, 

Clarissa

Hi ${user_firstname},

We would like to express our concern regarding this practice when there is a lack of necessary steps taken to ensure compliance with the respective privacy law. 

We aim to provide you with some important information:

* You are considered independent data controllers under privacy regulations. This means that you are responsible for ensuring that your use of CCTV cameras aligns with local and EU laws, particularly with regard to privacy and data protection.
* If you use CCTV cameras, we recommend that you ensure that you have the CCTV warning sign and enhance it by providing key details such as the purpose of the CCTV, the controller's name, the data retention period, and information on where customers can access a comprehensive CCTV privacy notice. This will help ensure transparency and compliance with privacy regulations.
* We encourage you to review your Privacy Notices and ensure that it outlines how personal data from CCTV is processed. 
* Kindly ensure that you inform customers about the processing of their personal data and CCTV records.
* Please share your Privacy Notice with us so we can send it to the customers and inform them about how their data is being used by you in this case. 

Please be aware that non-compliance with these requirements could potentially lead to legal consequences due to breaches of privacy laws.

While we offer these recommendations, we want to emphasize that as independent data controllers, you have the autonomy to decide whether to follow our advice. However, it's important to note that you are accountable for any violations.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. 

If you have any questions or concerns, please feel free to reach out to us.

Hey [~accountid:6102799e8c15ca006f26463a] ,

We have checked and calculations in the balance seems correct. Let me explain how it works:

We calculate the commission from net sale value but add VAT to the commission (7.5%) as it’s subject to VAT.

Let’s take [this order |https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/orders/133926672?cityId=136]as an example. You can see the net food amount is 5581.4. So we calculated the commission 5581.4 * 10% = 558.14. And then added 7% VAT on top of it to find 600. So, the calculation is:

Payout = 6000 gross food sum - 600 gross commission = 5400 

If the company was charged from Gross, then would have been:

Gross food sum 6000, net commission 6000 * 10% = 600. Gross commission 600 + 7.5% VAT = 645

Hi all, here is the feedback from the advisor:

_When we are talking about the Fiscalization Act, invoices must contain the following:_

* _Time at which the invoice was issued (hour and minute);_
* +_Name of the person (operator) at the cash register_+_;_
* _Name of the payment method - cash, cards, check, transfer account, other._

_So if the service provider issues an invoice for his services provided, the invoice must contain the information about the operator. This is the operator, the person who is responsible for the issuance of invoices and this person is also mentioned in the Internal Act for fiscalization (this can be his name, his initials as defined in the internal act on fiscalisation)._

_If the invoice is issued by a third person in the name of the service provider, then the OIB number of the service provider must be mentioned under Operator._

_There is no obligation to show the name of the eater (who ordered the food) on the invoice if we deal with B2C relationship._
